The right-hand bar inside each year shows the MAID death toll that year , scaled to 2024's 16,499. Watch it fill from a sliver in 2016 to nearly the full width in 2024. Bills get passed; the bar grows. Bills get defeated (e.g. C-233); the bar grows.

The bar fills regardless of which party is in power. Bill C-14 (2016) was passed by a Liberal majority. Bill C-233 (2024) was defeated by Liberal + Conservative + Bloc whip together. The procurement contracts to Israeli-tier suppliers were signed under the same Cabinets that announced the pause. The capture loop ( Flow C ) doesn't have a partisan colour because it was never about party — it was…

Bills that would have closed legs of the pipeline were defeated. Bill C-233 (arms export restriction): defeated 22–295. The Track 2 mental-illness MAID review: delayed three times, never repealed. Indigenous Services' drinking-water gap: $44B needed, $3.86B allocated. Each one of these is a recorded choice not to close a leg. That is the Article II intent test on a calendar.
The pipeline isn't a conspiracy. It's a calendar. The bills are public. The votes are public. The numbers are public. They thought nobody would put them in order.
Open the instrument. Atmosphere is not evidence.
